citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., and Fernández, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. arXiv:1606.06031.
creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández (CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento; Institute for Logic, Language & Computation, University of Amsterdam)
description: LAMBADA (LAnguage Modeling Broadened to Account for Discourse Aspects) is a dataset to evaluate computational models for text understanding via a word prediction task. It is a collection of narrative passages (from the BookCorpus) where human subjects can guess the last word when given the whole passage but not when given only the last sentence. The dataset consists of 10,022 passages (4,869 development and 5,153 test) requiring models to track information across broad discourse context.
name: LAMBADA
publisher: CIMeC - Center for Mind/Brain Sciences, University of Trento
rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 subjects guessed the target word from the whole passage (steps 1 and 2), plus up to 10 subjects attempted to guess from the target sentence only (step 3).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects evaluated passages through CrowdFlower in three steps: (1) one subject guessed the target word given the whole passage (context + target sentence); if correct, (2) a second subject also guessed from the whole passage; if also correct, (3) additional subjects tried to guess the target word from the target sentence only, with up to 3 guesses per subject, until the word was guessed or 10 unsuccessful guesses were reached. Only passages where no subject could guess the word from the sentence alone were included. Subjects in steps 1 and 2 were paid $0.22 per page (10 passages per page); subjects in step 3 were paid $0.15 per page (20 sentences per page). The same subject could not judge the same item in both passage and sentence conditions.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a strong bias toward proper nouns as target words (48% of target words), which are hugely over-represented compared to the input data distribution. Common nouns constitute over one third (37%) of target words. Verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are rare. The dataset also contains quoted direct speech significantly more often than the input items overall (71% of LAMBADA items vs. 61% of input items). More than 80% of LAMBADA passages include the target word in the context. The use of unpublished novels from BookCorpus was intentional to minimize the usefulness of general world knowledge and external resources.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from the BookCorpus (Zhu et al., 2015), containing unpublished novels. After duplicate removal and filtering out potentially offensive material with a stop word list, the corpus contained 5,325 novels and 465 million words. Novels were randomly divided into training and development+testing partitions. Passages were filtered using a combination of four language models (a pre-trained RNN and three models trained on BookCorpus: a 4-gram model, an RNN, and a feed-forward model) to exclude passages where the target word had probability above 0.00175 in any model. Remaining passages were evaluated by human subjects through CrowdFlower crowdsourcing in a three-step pipeline: (1) one subject guessed the target word from the whole passage; (2) if correct, a second subject also guessed from the whole passage; (3) if also correct, additional subjects tried to guess from the target sentence only (up to 10 unsuccessful guesses). Only passages passing all three steps were included. About 1 in 25 input examples passed all selection steps.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data is the BookCorpus (Zhu et al., 2015), a collection of unpublished novels. After duplicate removal and filtering out potentially offensive material with a stop word list, the corpus contains 5,325 novels and 465 million words.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset uses a strict hit-or-miss approach requiring exact word matches, which excludes passages where subjects provided plausible or synonymous continuations. The evaluation is described as preliminary and only a proof-of-concept study. The dataset is limited to narrative text from unpublished novels (BookCorpus), which may not generalize to other text genres. Cost considerations precluded using more subjects at stage 1, which could in principle improve filtering quality. Standard language models are bound to fail on LAMBADA by design, since one of the first filters was to choose passages where simple language models were failing.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The BookCorpus was preprocessed by removing duplicates and filtering out potentially offensive material using a stop word list. Passages were constructed with a context of minimum sentences cumulatively containing at least 50 tokens before the target sentence. Passages where the target word had probability above 0.00175 according to any of four language models were excluded. The vocabulary of models was restricted to the 60K most frequent words in the training set (covering 95% of target words in the development set).
rai:dataSocialImpact: LAMBADA is intended to stimulate the development of novel language models that genuinely capture non-local discourse phenomena in natural language. The authors hope it will encourage the computational community to develop models with genuine broad-context language understanding capabilities, which has broader implications for natural language processing and AI.
rai:dataUseCases: LAMBADA is intended as a challenging benchmark for evaluating computational models' ability to understand broad discourse context in natural language text, specifically via a word prediction task. It is proposed as a test set to encourage development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context. The authors also planned to announce a public competition based on the LAMBADA data.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Four language models were used to filter passages before human annotation: (1) a pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN) by Mikolov et al. (2011), (2) a standard 4-gram model trained on BookCorpus, (3) an RNN trained on BookCorpus, and (4) a feed-forward model trained on BookCorpus. Passages where the target word had probability above 0.00175 according to any of these models were excluded.
